title: Saturation numbers for joins with graphs containing isolated vertices
summary: A graph $G$ is $H$-saturated if $G$ contains no $H$-copy as a subgraph, but adding any edge between two non-adjacent vertices in $G$ creates a copy of $H$. The saturation number $\mathrm{sat}(n,H)$ is the minimum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $H$-saturated graph. Cameron and Puleo [Discrete Math. 345 (2022), 112867] showed that $\mathrm{sat}(n,K_1\vee F)\le n-1+\mathrm{sat}(n-1,F)$ for all $n>|V(F)|$. It is natural to ask when the equality holds.
